1 Welcome This project applies text analysis methods to several novels by Charles Dickens to explore writing style, chapter structure, vocabulary patterns, and statistical trends. The full report is organized as follows: 01-intro.Rmd – Introduction 02-data-prep.Rmd – Downloading and cleaning Dickens texts 03-descriptive-analysis.Rmd – Summary statistics and word analysis 04-regression-models.Rmd – Linear regression models and predictions 05-conclusion.Rmd – Key takeaways 06-citations.Rmd – References

3 Introduction This book explores the writing style of Charles Dickens using three of his public-domain novels: A Tale of Two Cities Great Expectations Oliver Twist The goals of the project are: Download and prepare clean text data using R. Perform descriptive text analysis (frequencies, chapters, patterns). Use linear regression to test whether Dickens shows consistent chapter structure, such as: Words per chapter Sentences per chapter Words per sentence Visualize Dickens’s writing patterns using multiple plots. 4 Conclusion This project analyzed three novels by Charles Dickens using text mining techniques in R. Key findings: Dickens shows strong consistency in chapter length across books. His vocabulary patterns (top words and stems) show a clear author signature. Linear regression confirms: Words per chapter follow a predictable pattern. Sentence structure is similar across books. Words per sentence cluster in a narrow range. Overall, Dickens demonstrates a stable and structured writing style across novels, making his works ideal for text-based statistical analysis.
